content.value_statement: React view transitions are easy to misplace, causing silent or noisy animations. This skill guides route, Suspense, list, and shared element animation choices.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to animate route, state, Suspense, list, and shared element changes.
Provides a workflow for auditing navigation paths and placing ViewTransition boundaries.
Includes CSS recipes for fade, slide, morph, scale, persistent elements, and reduced motion.
Covers Next.js App Router setup, link transition types, and loading boundary reveals.
Warns about common placement, naming, and default animation mistakes.
limitations: It provides guidance and snippets; it does not run visual tests by itself.
React ViewTransition availability depends on React and browser support.
Next.js link transition support depends on the project version and experimental flag.
It cannot guarantee animation quality without app-specific review.

use_cases.title: Add route motion
use_cases.description: Plan and implement directional transitions between list, detail, and ordered sequence pages.

use_cases.title: Standardize Next.js animations
use_cases.description: Apply App Router view transition patterns across pages, links, loading states, and shared elements.

use_cases.title: Document motion rules
use_cases.description: Create consistent guidance for fades, slides, shared elements, reduced motion, and animation boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Add basic transitions
prompt_templates.prompt: Add basic enter and exit animations to this React component. Use the skill guidance and explain where the ViewTransition boundary belongs.

prompt_templates.title: Animate navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this route change flow and add directional navigation transitions only where spatial depth is clear.

prompt_templates.title: Create shared elements
prompt_templates.prompt: Create shared element transitions between this list view and detail view. Keep names unique and include fallback behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Next.js app
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js App Router project for route transitions, Suspense reveals, persistent elements, and reduced motion support.

output_examples.input: Add a detail-page animation from a gallery card.
output_examples.output: A route map, nav-forward and nav-back behavior, a shared image name, and a note to keep the header isolated.

output_examples.input: Improve loading state animation for a server-rendered grid.
output_examples.output: A Suspense reveal plan with fallback exit, content enter, default suppression, and reduced motion coverage.
Findings about layout-level boundaries, duplicate shared names, and places where directional slides should become fades.

best_practices: Audit navigation paths, Suspense boundaries, and persistent elements before editing.
Use default="none" and enable only the triggers that communicate intent.
Pair shared element names carefully and keep them globally unique.
anti_patterns: Do not wrap layouts with directional transitions when pages need enter and exit.
Do not use directional slides for unordered lateral navigation.
Do not rely on raw viewTransitionName to trigger React transitions.

faq.question: What does this skill help implement?
faq.answer: It helps implement React view transitions for route changes, Suspense reveals, list reorders, and shared elements.

faq.question: Does it support Next.js?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers App Router setup, link transition types, loading boundaries, Server Components, and programmatic navigation.

faq.question: Does it replace animation libraries?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on the browser View Transition API through React and related CSS pseudo-elements.

faq.question: Can it handle shared element transitions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains named ViewTransition pairs, unique names, fallback behavior, and list identity composition.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires reduced motion CSS and explains when animations should stay silent.

faq.question: Will it test animations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives implementation guidance, but visual verification still depends on the project and browser.
